cricket_protocol/models.py:55
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Normalize the constructed `Wicket` instance.**

If code calls `Wicket(kind="none", umpire_confirmed=True)`, this validator returns a copy rather than `self`. Pydantic does not support returning a different instance from a top-level after-validator during `__init__`; the constructed wicket can retain `umpire_confirmed=True`. Set the validated field to `False` on `self`, return `self`, and add a direct-construction regression test. ([docs.pydantic.dev](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/validators/))

schemas/ball_event.schema.json:53
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Align the schema default with `Wicket`'s kind-dependent behavior.**

When `umpire_confirmed` is omitted, `Wicket` sets it to `false` for `kind: "none"` and to `true` for dismissal kinds. The schema publishes an unconditional `default: true`, which can give schema-based consumers the wrong value for non-dismissals. Remove the unconditional default or encode the kind-dependent rule in the schema.

The stats producer emits totals only, but `fantasy/app.py` does not fetch that producer. It accepts `last_ball` from the request body and passes it to `settle`.
